To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the time course of RSR responses to hemodynamic changes is determined by the rate at which the kidney releases renin in response the autoregulation of renal vascular caliber.
renal hemodynamic changes cause changes in renin secretion and that the time course of these changes depends on the type of hemodynamic changes.
Renin secretion in response to a change in renal blood flow depends upon the time course of the renal vasodilation or vasoconstriction that follows the flow change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control renin secretion and the effects of renin on renal function.
the mechanisms by which the kidney regulates its own blood flow.
the effects of renal vascular caliber on the release of renin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the renin secretion rate is determined by the balance of the opposing effects of the renal perfusion pressure and renal vascular resistance.
renin secretion is a function of the renal vascular caliber, but the time course of the changes in renin secretion is not simply a function of the time course of renal vascular caliber.
the time course of RSR is a composite of the time course of the renal conductance response and the time course of release of stored renin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
renin release is a response to renal vasodilation.
the renal vascular caliber plays an important role in the regulation of RSR, and that the neurohumoral factors are also involved in the control of renin secretion.

renal hemodynamic alterations, especially autoregulatory vasodilatation, play a major role in the release of renin from the juxtaglomerular cells, but that neurohumoral factors also contribute to renin release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time constant for the changes in renal conductance is shorter than that for the changes in renin secretion.
the time course of RSR is determined by the kinetics of renin release, which in turn is related to the kinetics of renal vasodilation.
the kidney is a highly sensitive organ that can respond rapidly to changes in blood flow and perfusion pressure.
